ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle CAB=90^\circ$. Three squares are constructed on the sides of $\triangle ABC$. A line is drawn from point H perpendicular to $ED$ at point J, and $HE$ is connected. Extend $HE$ to intersect $FC$ at point K. If $K$ is the midpoint of $FC$, and the area of $\triangle ABC$ minus the area of $\triangle EHJ$ equals 16, then what is the length of $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $HJ$ and $FC$ to intersect at point N.\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral $EABD$ is a square and $HJ\perp ED$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral $ECNJ$ is a rectangle.\\
$\therefore$ $CE=NJ$, $EJ=CN$.\\
$CE\parallel HN$, $ED\parallel CN$.\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ECH=\angle MHN$.\\
$\because$ $\angle ECH+\angle BCA=90^\circ$ and $\angle CBA+\angle BCA=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ECH=\angle CBA$.\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CBA=\angle MHN$.\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle HCN\cong \triangle BCA$.\\
$\therefore$ $CN=CA$, $HN=AB$.\\
Let $CN=CA=a$, $HN=AB=b$.\\
$\therefore$ $CE=b-a$, $HJ=HN-JN=b-(b-a)=a$.\\
$\therefore$ $HJ=EJ=a$.\\
$\therefore$ $\angle HEJ=45^\circ$.\\
Also, $\because$ $ED\parallel KN$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EKC=45^\circ$.\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle EKC$ is an isosceles right triangle.\\
$\therefore$ $CK=CE=b-a$.\\
$\because$ K is the midpoint of $CF$, we have $CK=\frac{1}{2}a$.\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}a=b-a$.\\
$\therefore$ $b=\frac{3}{2}a$.\\
$\because$ ${S}_{\triangle ABC}-{S}_{\triangle EHJ}=16$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}\times a\times b-\frac{1}{2}a^2=16$.\\
$\therefore$ Solving gives $a=8$.\\
$\therefore$ $b=\frac{3}{2}\times 8=\boxed{12}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle CAB=90^\circ$. Three squares are constructed on the sides of $\triangle ABC$. A line is drawn from point H perpendicular to $ED$ at point J, and $HE$ is connected. Extend $HE$ to intersect $FC$ at point K. If $K$ is the midpoint of $FC$, and the area of $\triangle ABC$ minus the area of $\triangle EHJ$ equals 16, then what is the length of $AB$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $HJ$ and $FC$ to intersect at point N.\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral $EABD$ is a square and $HJ\perp ED$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral $ECNJ$ is a rectangle.\\
$\therefore$ $CE=NJ$, $EJ=CN$.\\
$CE\parallel HN$, $ED\parallel CN$.\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ECH=\angle MHN$.\\
$\because$ $\angle ECH+\angle BCA=90^\circ$ and $\angle CBA+\angle BCA=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ECH=\angle CBA$.\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CBA=\angle MHN$.\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle HCN\cong \triangle BCA$.\\
$\therefore$ $CN=CA$, $HN=AB$.\\
Let $CN=CA=a$, $HN=AB=b$.\\
$\therefore$ $CE=b-a$, $HJ=HN-JN=b-(b-a)=a$.\\
$\therefore$ $HJ=EJ=a$.\\
$\therefore$ $\angle HEJ=45^\circ$.\\
Also, $\because$ $ED\parallel KN$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EKC=45^\circ$.\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle EKC$ is an isosceles right triangle.\\
$\therefore$ $CK=CE=b-a$.\\
$\because$ K is the midpoint of $CF$, we have $CK=\frac{1}{2}a$.\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}a=b-a$.\\
$\therefore$ $b=\frac{3}{2}a$.\\
$\because$ ${S}_{\triangle ABC}-{S}_{\triangle EHJ}=16$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}\times a\times b-\frac{1}{2}a^2=16$.\\
$\therefore$ Solving gives $a=8$.\\
$\therefore$ $b=\frac{3}{2}\times 8=\boxed{12}$
